name: Outlook (Microsoft 365 / Outlook.com via Microsoft Graph)
summary: Registering a multitenant Entra app and connecting your own mailbox takes ~20 minutes and there is no Microsoft app review. Publisher verification (free, via a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account) is fast once Partner Center vetting clears, which can take days to weeks. What matters most: in tenants on 'Let Microsoft manage your consent settings' (the default for new tenants), Microsoft's managed consent policy stops end users from consenting to Mail.*/Calendars.*/MailboxSettings.* scopes for any app, verified or not (mail and calendar scopes were added around Nov 2025), so plan on a tenant admin consenting for each customer org.

verdict.label: Admin consent
verdict.headline: No Microsoft app review, but tenants on Microsoft's managed default consent policy need an admin to approve Mail/Calendar scopes for each customer org. Verification alone does not lift that.

timeline.first_connection: 15-30 minutes (your own tenant or a personal Outlook.com account)
timeline.production: Personal Outlook.com accounts: same day (an unverified label may show). Work/school accounts: 1-3 days for publisher verification if Partner Center is already vetted, 1-4+ weeks if Partner Center vetting is new or stalls. After that, each customer org may still need its admin to consent.
timeline.hands_on_effort: 2-4 hours (app registration, redirect/secret config, domain verification, Partner Center enrollment, admin-consent onboarding page)
timeline.wait_detail: Microsoft does not review the app itself. The waits are (1) Partner Center legal-business/employment verification for the CPP account, often days but community reports of weeks to months, (2) DNS propagation for publisher-domain verification, and (3) each customer tenant's admin approving consent. That last one is outside your control and is the real driver of time-to-value for B2B.

approval.type: brand/consent verification (publisher verification) + per-tenant admin consent
approval.trigger: A multitenant app (registered after Nov 8 2020) asking users in other tenants for permissions beyond sign-in/profile. Separately, for every app (not only multitenant ones), Mail.*, Calendars.*, MailboxSettings.*, Contacts.ReadWrite, Contacts.*.Shared, Tasks.*, People.Read and EAS/EWS/IMAP/POP access are excluded from end-user consent in tenants still on the Microsoft-managed default consent policy ('Let Microsoft manage your consent settings').
approval.what_happens_without_it: Unverified: with risk-based step-up consent, users in other tenants cannot consent and get a risky/unverified-publisher warning. Tenants that allow only verified-publisher apps block you outright. Even when verified: tenants on the Microsoft-managed default policy, or with user consent disabled, show 'Need admin approval' and require an admin grant via /adminconsent or the admin consent workflow. Personal Microsoft accounts are not governed by tenant consent policies.
approval.cost: Free. Publisher verification and CPP enrollment have no fee. Optional Microsoft 365 Certification needs a paid third-party audit (contract with Claranet); the price is not published.

managed_option.when_you_need_your_own: Use your own Entra app once users should see your name (not Composio's) on the Microsoft consent screen, when you need custom scopes or your own throttling budget (Outlook limits are per app per mailbox), or when customer admins must grant tenant-wide consent to an app published by your verified organization. Point the redirect URI at Composio's callback (https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback) if you stay on Composio. Existing connections stay on the old auth config until users re-auth.

prerequisites.item: A Microsoft Entra work/school tenant where you hold Application Developer or Application Administrator rights
prerequisites.why: Apps registered with a personal Microsoft account can't be publisher verified (MSANotSupported), and creating apps outside a directory is deprecated. A free Entra tenant is fine.

prerequisites.item: A DNS-verified custom domain in that tenant, matching your company email domain
prerequisites.why: The email domain used in CPP verification must match the app's publisher domain or be a DNS-verified custom domain in the tenant; *.onmicrosoft.com does not qualify.

prerequisites.item: Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program (formerly MPN) account, Partner Global Account, fully vetted
prerequisites.why: Its Partner One ID is what publisher verification attaches to the app. It must be the partner global account (PGA) ID, not a location ID, and the app's tenant must be associated with the PGA. Verification is free.

prerequisites.item: MFA on the admin user who performs verification
prerequisites.why: Verification fails with InteractionRequired unless MFA was performed in the same session.

prerequisites.item: A test M365 tenant with an Exchange Online mailbox (for example a Microsoft 365 Developer Program sandbox, if eligible) plus a personal Outlook.com account
prerequisites.why: So you can test both account types and the admin-consent path.

phases.name: Create the app
phases.goal: A multitenant app registration with a client ID and secret

steps.title: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center with a work/school account
steps.detail: Entra ID > App registrations > New registration. The console is a SPA: curl returns 403 without a browser user agent and 200 (app shell) with one, and sign-in happens client-side.

steps.title: Choose supported account types
steps.detail: For an agent product serving both businesses and consumers, pick 'Accounts in any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts' (signInAudience AzureADandPersonalMicrosoftAccount). This caps redirect URIs at 100 and disallows query strings and wildcards in them. If you only serve businesses, pick 'any organizational directory' (multitenant). Single-tenant won't work for external customers.

steps.title: Add a Web platform redirect URI
steps.detail: Use an exact https URI such as https://app.example.com/oauth/microsoft/callback. http is allowed only for localhost/127.0.0.1, where the port is ignored for matching. Max 256 characters. URIs are case-sensitive.

steps.title: Create a client secret (or, better, upload a certificate)
steps.detail: Certificates & secrets. Copy the secret value immediately. Secrets expire, so put rotation on a calendar.

steps.title: Add delegated Microsoft Graph permissions
steps.detail: openid, profile, offline_access, User.Read, Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Send, Calendars.ReadWrite (plus Contacts.Read and MailboxSettings.Read if needed). All are delegated with 'Admin consent required: No' in Graph's reference, but see the tenant consent-policy gotcha. Don't add application permissions to an end-user agent.

steps.title: Fill in branding: name, logo, home page, terms of service, privacy statement
steps.detail: Branding & properties. These show on the consent screen and admins look at them.

phases.name: Configure & test
phases.goal: Complete a real connection with a work account and a personal account

steps.title: Implement auth code flow with PKCE against the /common endpoint
steps.detail: Authorize: https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/authorize. Token: .../common/oauth2/v2.0/token. Both confirmed via the live discovery document. Request offline_access or you get no refresh token. Use S256 PKCE (recommended for confidential clients too). Use /organizations or /consumers to restrict account type.

steps.title: Connect your own tenant mailbox and a personal Outlook.com mailbox
steps.detail: The /consumers path redirects to login.live.com (seen live). Your home tenant can consent under its own policy. Then call GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/messages, which returns 401 InvalidAuthenticationToken without a token.

steps.title: Test from a second (customer-like) tenant, both as a normal user and as an admin
steps.detail: Expect 'Need admin approval' for Mail/Calendar scopes as a normal user in a tenant on default settings. Build an onboarding path that sends the customer's admin to https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant|organizations}/v2.0/adminconsent?client_id=...&scope=https://graph.microsoft.com/Mail.ReadWrite ...&redirect_uri=...

steps.title: Handle throttling and token refresh
steps.detail: Outlook allows 10,000 requests per 10 min per app per mailbox, 4 concurrent requests, and 150 MB of uploads per 5 min. Back off on 429. Refresh tokens last 90 days by default (24h for SPA redirect types) and roll on every use. Store the newest one.

phases.name: Get production-ready (publisher verification + customer consent)
phases.goal: A blue 'verified' badge and a repeatable admin-consent onboarding for customer tenants
phases.duration: 1 day to several weeks (dominated by Partner Center vetting)

steps.title: Verify your custom domain in the Entra tenant and set it as the app's publisher domain
steps.detail: DNS TXT record. Can't be *.onmicrosoft.com. The email domain used in CPP verification must match the app's publisher domain or be a DNS-verified custom domain in the tenant, or you'll hit PublisherDomainMismatch.

steps.title: Enroll in the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program and complete verification
steps.detail: Sign in at partner.microsoft.com with a user from the same tenant. Provide your legal business profile; email and employment verification follow. Use the partner global account (PGA) Partner One ID; a location ID will not work. Associate the app's tenant with the PGA, and register the app with a work/school account.

steps.title: Microsoft vets the Partner Center account
steps.detail: No SLA published. Microsoft says developers who already meet the requirements 'can be verified in minutes', but forum threads report weeks to months of stuck or looping verification with little feedback.

steps.title: Add the Partner One ID to the app (Branding & properties > Publisher verification)
steps.detail: Needs Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator in Entra plus CPP Partner Admin or Account Admin in Partner Center, and MFA in the same session. Can also be done via POST /applications/{objectId}/setVerifiedPublisher.

steps.title: Ship an admin-consent onboarding flow and docs for customer IT
steps.detail: A 'Connect your organization' button that hits /adminconsent, an explanation of every scope, and instructions for approving via the admin consent workflow. Expect tenants still on the Microsoft-managed default policy to need this for any app, verified or not.

steps.title: (Optional) Publisher Attestation, then Microsoft 365 Certification
steps.detail: Attestation is a self-assessment that Microsoft says usually takes about an hour. Certification is a yearly independent audit including pen testing, under contract with Claranet. Neither is required for Graph OAuth, but both help with enterprise security reviews.
steps.effort: Attestation ~1 hour; certification weeks + paid audit

config.redirect_uri_rules: Exact match, case-sensitive, https required except localhost/127.0.0.1 (port ignored for localhost). Max 256 characters each. Up to 256 URIs for work-only apps, 100 if personal accounts are included. No query strings or wildcards when personal accounts are enabled. No IPv6 loopback.
config.pkce: Supported (S256 and plain). Recommended for all clients, required for SPA redirect types.
config.refresh_tokens: Only issued with offline_access. 90-day default lifetime for web and native apps, 24h for SPA redirect URIs. Each use returns a new refresh token; keep the newest. Revoked on password change for some flows, on admin revocation, or on user revocation. Access tokens last about 1 hour (expires_in 3599 in the docs' example).

scopes.note: User-consentable everywhere. offline_access is needed for refresh tokens.
Graph lists 'Admin consent required: No' and it's consentable by personal accounts, but it's excluded from user consent under the Microsoft-managed default policy.
Not on the Microsoft-managed exclusion list as of the Learn page updated 2026-08-28. Tenant custom policies may still block it.
Excluded from user consent under the Microsoft-managed policy.

scopes.tier: Read user-consentable; ReadWrite admin in default-policy tenants
scopes.note: Only Contacts.ReadWrite and the *.Shared variants are on the exclusion list.
Excluded from user consent under the Microsoft-managed policy.
Always need admin consent. Not appropriate for a per-user agent.

gotchas.title: The default consent policy blocks end-user consent to Mail/Calendar scopes
gotchas.detail: 'Let Microsoft manage your consent settings' is the default for new tenants. It lets users consent to any user-consentable delegated permission except a list that, per Learn (updated 2026-08-28), includes Mail.*, Calendars.*, MailBoxSettings.*, Contacts.ReadWrite, Contacts.*.Shared, Tasks.*, People.Read and EAS/EWS/IMAP/POP (Files/Sites.* are also excluded); Contacts.Read and Mail.Send are not listed. The rule applies to every app on a user-consent request, not only multitenant apps, but only in tenants still on the Microsoft-managed setting. Timeline per secondary blogs: the mid-2025 rollout blocked only Files.Read(Write).All and Sites.Read(Write).All; mail, calendar, mailbox and Teams scopes were added around Nov 2025, and Contacts/Tasks/People-type scopes in 2026. There is no verified-publisher exemption; the only exemption is a separate Microsoft policy for named mail clients (Apple Mail, Spark, eM Client, Thunderbird, etc.). So in these tenants an admin must consent for an Outlook agent; point users at the admin consent workflow.

gotchas.title: Unverified multitenant apps can't get user consent in other tenants
gotchas.detail: For apps registered after Nov 8 2020 with risk-based step-up consent enabled, users in other tenants can't consent to permissions beyond basic sign-in/profile for an unverified publisher, and they see a risky-app warning.

gotchas.title: You need a work/school tenant and a non-onmicrosoft domain
gotchas.detail: Apps registered with a personal Microsoft account can't be verified (MSANotSupported). An app can't be moved between tenants, so register in your company's real tenant from day one.

gotchas.title: Partner Center vetting is the unpredictable wait
gotchas.detail: There's no SLA. Forum reports describe verification loops, unexplained rejections and support going silent. Start CPP enrollment on day 1, in parallel with building.

gotchas.title: Personal accounts change redirect-URI rules
gotchas.detail: Including personal Microsoft accounts removes support for query strings and wildcards in redirect URIs and lowers the maximum to 100.

gotchas.title: Throttling is per app per mailbox
gotchas.detail: 10,000 requests per 10 minutes and 4 concurrent requests per mailbox. Agents that fan out parallel calls to one mailbox will hit 429s. Batches send at most 4 requests in parallel.

gotchas.title: SPA-type redirect URIs get 24-hour refresh tokens
gotchas.detail: Register the callback as 'Web' (confidential server) to get 90-day rolling refresh tokens for background agent work.

gotchas.title: Admins can still block you after consent
gotchas.detail: Admins can require user assignment (which forces admin consent), restrict mailbox scope with application access policies or RBAC for app-only access, or disable user consent entirely.

blockers.symptom: Users see 'Need admin approval' / 'needs permission to access resources in your organization that only an admin can grant'
blockers.what_to_do: Expected for Mail/Calendar scopes in default-policy tenants. Send the customer admin to /{tenant}/v2.0/adminconsent, or ask them to enable the admin consent workflow and approve the request.

blockers.symptom: Consent screen shows 'unverified' and a risky-app warning, and users in other tenants can't proceed
blockers.what_to_do: Complete publisher verification (Partner One ID on the app).

Use the PartnerGlobal ID (not a location ID). Make sure the tenant is associated in CPP tenant management, your user holds Partner Admin/Account Admin, and the legal business profile shows 'authorized'.

Make the email domain used in CPP verification match the app's publisher domain, or verify it as a custom domain in Entra and set it as the app's publisher domain (*.onmicrosoft.com does not qualify).

blockers.symptom: InteractionRequired, UserUnableToAddPublisher or UnableToAddPublisher during verification
blockers.what_to_do: Do MFA in the same session. Remediate any risky-user state. If flagged as a risky request, retry the next day.
Register the exact redirect URI (case, path, trailing slash) on the app object.

blockers.symptom: Token endpoint returns invalid_grant AADSTS9002313 or invalid_client AADSTS700026
blockers.what_to_do: Malformed or expired code/PKCE verifier, or the client has no matching secret or certificate. Re-run authorize and check the credentials. Both error shapes were seen live with dummy values.

blockers.symptom: Partner Center verification stuck 'pending' for weeks
blockers.what_to_do: Open a Partner Center support ticket with reference IDs, and escalate via Partner Compliance forums. Keep testing in the meantime with your own tenant and personal accounts.

agent_can: Generate the app manifest settings (signInAudience, redirect URIs, requiredResourceAccess for Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Send, Calendars.ReadWrite, offline_access)
Implement the MSAL / raw auth code + PKCE flow, token refresh with rotation, and 429 backoff respecting 4 concurrent requests per mailbox
Build the /adminconsent onboarding route and the 'Need admin approval' detection and messaging
Draft the privacy statement and terms sections on mailbox data use, plus a per-scope justification sheet for customer IT/security reviews
Draft Publisher Attestation questionnaire answers from your architecture docs
Probe endpoints and decode errors (AADSTS codes) during testing
you_must: Sign in to Entra with a work/school account and create the registration and secret
Add the DNS TXT record to verify your company domain
Enroll in the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program with your legal business details and complete email/employment verification
Hold the Entra and Partner Center admin roles, perform MFA, and attach the Partner One ID
Get customer tenant admins to grant consent (sales/IT relationship)
Decide on, and pay for, Microsoft 365 Certification if enterprise customers require it

uncertainties: Which tenants actually run the Microsoft-managed consent policy. Learn says it's the default for new tenants; tenants with custom or legacy settings are unaffected. The rollout dates (Files/Sites mid-2025, mail/calendar/mailbox/Teams around Nov 2025, Contacts/Tasks/People-type in 2026) come from secondary blogs (topedia, Nov 2025 and May 2026); the Microsoft message center posts could not be reached on 2026-10-27. We couldn't see what share of real customer tenants it covers.

As of the Learn page updated 2026-08-28 (re-checked 2026-10-27), the exclusion list names Mail.*, Calendars.*, MailBoxSettings.*, Contacts.ReadWrite, Contacts.*.Shared, Tasks.*, People.Read and EAS/EWS/IMAP/POP, but not Mail.Send or Contacts.Read. Microsoft can change a managed policy without notice. Re-check the list before launch.
Whether risk-based step-up consent is still active in the same form in 2026. The publisher verification page still cites the Nov 2020 rule (page updated 2026-06-15).
Partner Center vetting time has no SLA. Estimates are from community threads and range from same day to months.

Personal (MSA) consent experience for unverified apps: we inferred that tenant consent policies don't apply and that users see an unverified label but can consent. We couldn't confirm this without an account.

The authorize probe returned a sign-in page (sErrorCode 50059/50058) instead of an explicit 'application not found' (AADSTS700016), because the client is validated only after sign-in. We couldn't observe the post-login error without credentials.
Client secret maximum lifetime (the portal offers up to 24 months) is from model knowledge, not a page read in this session.
Composio supports Outlook with managed auth according to its general docs. We didn't read the Outlook-specific toolkit page.

meta.reviewed: On 2026-10-27 fact-checkers re-verified the Microsoft-managed consent policy (B1, partly) and publisher-verification requirements (B2, confirmed). Corrected the policy timeline (mail/calendar scopes added around Nov 2025, not mid-2025) and its scope (every app, only in tenants on the Microsoft-managed setting), and added PGA/domain details; rollout dates still rest on secondary blogs because the Microsoft message center posts were unreachable.
